name: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2P

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for CMT2P

criteria.description: Progressive distal muscle weakness and atrophy predominantly affecting lower limbs
Electrophysiological evidence of axonal neuropathy with reduced compound muscle action potentials
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the LRSAM1 gene
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Nerve biopsy showing axonal degeneration without significant demyelination

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive distal muscle weakness and atrophy with electrophysiological evidence of axonal neuropathy plus identification of pathogenic LRSAM1 mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic confirmation is essential for definitive diagnosis; clinical presentation may overlap with other CMT subtypes.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Distal muscle weakness and atrophy of lower limbs
Reduced or absent deep tendon reflexes
Sensory loss predominantly affecting distal lower limbs
searchTerms: loss of feeling in lower legs
foot shape abnormalities like high arches

common.symptomName: Steppage gait due to foot drop
searchTerms: steppage gait due to foot drop

common.symptomName: Mild distal sensory neuropathy with impaired vibration and proprioception
searchTerms: mild numbness affecting vibration and position sense in hands and feet
early sensory nerve damage with impaired balance and vibration
distal sensory neuropathy with reduced vibration sense
burning pain in hands and feet
nerve pain in fingers and toes
difficulty breathing due to muscle weakness

laboratory: Elevated creatine kinase may be mild or absent
imaging: MRI may show muscle atrophy in distal limbs
Nerve ultrasound may reveal nerve enlargement
other: Electromyography showing reduced amplitude of motor responses consistent with axonal neuropathy
Nerve conduction studies demonstrating normal or mildly reduced conduction velocities

distinguishingFeatures: Demyelinating neuropathy with markedly slowed nerve conduction velocities
Recurrent focal neuropathies triggered by pressure
Asymmetric distal weakness without sensory loss

redFlags: Rapid progression of weakness over weeks
Bulbar muscle involvement or respiratory failure
references: Lupski JR et al. Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2P: clinical and genetic features. Neurology. 2010.
Rossor AM, Polke JM, Houlden H, Reilly MM. Clinical implications of genetic advances in Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease. Nat Rev Neurol. 2013.
